query: What factors explain low review scores?

per_column.name: summary_length
per_column.rationale: Generic surface feature of the text; not a candidate cause of low scores nor a common cause of any treatment and the outcome. Descriptive noise.

per_column.name: text_length
per_column.rationale: Mechanical length metric with no clear causal relation to satisfaction; not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: has_negative_words
per_column.rationale: Negative wording is an expression of the (dis)satisfaction that also produces the low score; it lies on the path from the underlying experience to the outcome rather than being an exogenous cause. Effectively a proxy/mediator of the outcome, not a confounder.

per_column.name: has_positive_words
per_column.rationale: Same reasoning: positive wording reflects the same latent sentiment that drives the score. Adjusting for it conflates outcome with predictor.

per_column.name: helpfulness_ratio
per_column.rationale: Helpfulness votes are determined AFTER and partly BY the review content and score; it is a downstream consequence, so conditioning on it risks collider bias, not confounding.

per_column.name: has_complaint_markers
per_column.rationale: Complaint language is a manifestation of dissatisfaction that co-occurs with the low score; on the causal path from experience to outcome, not a common cause.

per_column.name: uppercase_ratio
per_column.rationale: Stylistic emphasis feature; at best a weak proxy of emotional tone (thus mediator-like), not an independent common cause of a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: exclamation_count
per_column.rationale: Punctuation/emphasis proxy for affect; reflects sentiment rather than causing the score. Not a genuine confounder.

per_column.name: question_count
per_column.rationale: Surface punctuation feature; no clear common-cause relationship to any treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: is_low_score
per_column.rationale: This is the focus outcome itself, derived from Score; not a covariate.

judge.rationale: The added columns are mechanical text features (lengths, punctuation counts, uppercase ratio) plus lexical sentiment proxies (has_negative/positive_words, complaint_markers) and one downstream helpfulness measure. None of these is a well-defined TREATMENT whose effect on low scores is being attributed, nor a genuine CONFOUNDER that is a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome. The sentiment/complaint columns are expressions of the same latent (dis)satisfaction that produces the score (mediators/outcome proxies), and helpfulness_ratio is a post-outcome collider. No exogenous common cause (e.g., product quality/category, price, delivery/shipping issue, reviewer harshness, product age) was surfaced. The set fails the causal-estimation test: no treatment identified and no genuine confounders adjusted for.
